Command: Slaughter and Sacrifice Only at the Sanctuary
Summary: What man soever killeth an ox, lamb, or goat in the camp and bringeth it not to the tabernacle door is cut off — and they shall no more offer their sacrifices unto devils. This Leviticus 17 centralization law is outside every live row's range (Sacrifices covers Leviticus 1-7; Priesthood covers Leviticus 8-10).
Commandment: Do not slaughter sacrificial animals in the open field or sacrifice to goat-demons; bring every offering to the tabernacle door.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The New Testament gives the reason the centralization ended: the one sacrifice of Christ replaced the many, and worship is no longer bound to one place (John 4:21-24; Hebrews 10:11-14). Sacrifices to goat-demons and private altars were the exact rivals this law excluded.
Purpose: Scripture's stated reason: that they may no more offer their sacrifices unto devils, after whom they have gone a whoring (Leviticus 17:7).
